text: On the other hand, Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked whether cybersecurity freelancers need to be regulated, while some Members − Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Ms Joan Peirera − spoke about the missed opportunity and risks of not regulating individual cybersecurity professionals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: On the one hand, there is a call for even individual professionals to be regulated while, on the other hand, some expressed concerns over potential cost implications for businesses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As I had mentioned in my opening speech, for a start, the licensing framework is deliberately light touch in view of the need to strike a good balance between industry development and cybersecurity needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Furthermore, given the global nature of the cybersecurity industry, we recognise there are currently practical challenges to require individual cybersecurity professionals to be licensed, especially for service providers who deploy employees from overseas to serve clients in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Nonetheless, other cybersecurity services will still need to comply with other laws in Singapore, such as CMA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, we do not intend to require companies to be licensed for providing such services to their related companies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Under the Bill, no person may engage in the business of providing any licensable cybersecurity service to other persons, except under and in accordance with a licence granted or renewed under clause 26.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CSA will encourage consumers of such cybersecurity services to only procure services from licensed cybersecurity service providers by publishing a list of licensees online.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Companies can also inform CSA of any unlicensed service providers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The proposed licensing framework is intended to reduce the safety and security risks that cybersecurity service providers can pose.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The service providers are required to ensure that their key executive officers are fit and proper persons when applying for a licence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Any applicant who is not fit and proper may be refused a licence under clause 26.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Similarly, a cybersecurity service provider’s licence may be revoked or suspended, if the service provider is no longer fit and proper, among other factors under clause 30.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Henry Kwek also asked whether the Government could create a certification system that favours cybersecurity professionals who have a vested interest in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CSA intends to work with the industry and professional association partners to establish voluntary accreditation and certification regimes for cybersecurity service providers and professionals to raise the quality of cybersecurity services and further improve their standing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For example, in partnership with CSA and the Association of Information Security Professionals (AISP), the Council for Registered Ethical Security Testers (CREST), a non-profit international organisation, established a Singapore chapter to introduce penetration testing certifications and accreditation in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Given the nascent nature of our industry, we should remain open and take reference from internationally recognised standards where possible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It would not be in our interest to favour only those professionals who have a vested interest in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Likewise, we would want our local cybersecurity professionals to be recognised in other markets, based on their professional expertise and experience.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The regulatory regime needs to strike a balance between security needs and the development of a vibrant cybersecurity ecosystem.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is the best balance that we can find at this point in time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MCI and CSA will be engaging the industry in working out the implementation details for licensing, including licensing conditions for licensable cybersecurity service providers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will also continue to take in feedback from the industry on the licensing regime as the cybersecurity ecosystem evolves.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Several Members, Mr Zaqy Mohamad, Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Desmond Choo, asked about the Government’s plans to grow and develop the pool of cybersecurity professionals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Government is collaborating with the industry to grow the cybersecurity workforce in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked about the potential to build greater synergy in civilian and military cybersecurity capabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Today, CSA already works closely with MINDEF on cybersecurity matters.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For example, CSA can call on MINDEF for support when responding to cybersecurity incidents, as MINDEF is part of NCIRT.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CSA and MINDEF also collaborate in areas, such as the sharing of operational lessons and threat information, technology cooperation and participation in joint exercises, such as Exercise CYBER KNIGHTS 2017.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Last year, MINDEF announced the establishment of a new Cyber Defence vocation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I understand that they are looking into better harnessing the cybersecurity skills of National Servicemen (NSmen) to defend our military networks and contribute to the national cybersecurity effort.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CSA and MINDEF will continue to find more ways to cooperate in these areas.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I also agree with Mr Patrick Tay that we need to bring together various partners to assist cybersecurity professionals in areas, such as continual learning and career development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We need to continually upgrade our cybersecurity defences and training as cyberattacks are getting more sophisticated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CSA, through its Academy, is leading efforts to boost the skills of cybersecurity professionals working in the Government and CII sectors, such as energy and healthcare.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: On this, Sir, I look forward to the Labour Movement’s support.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ms Sun Xueling asked how the Bill would take into account global developments and evolving standards to tackle cybersecurity threats, while Mr Azmoon Ahmad spoke about the need to regularly review the regulatory framework, given the fast-changing Internet landscape.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In formulating this Bill, we studied cybersecurity legislation which other countries have implemented or are considering.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our Bill has taken into consideration these international developments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: During the implementation of the Bill, we will take reference from internationally recognised standards when developing codes of practice and standards of performance for the different sectors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We also recognise that the environment that we operate in may change with changes in the industry and technological trends.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Therefore, we will need to keep abreast of international developments, and review and adjust our laws to address new and emerging issues moving forward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan asked what MCI and CSA have done with respect to cybersecurity internationally and regionally.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CSA has been an active participant at international forums and discussions to develop international cyber norms, including at the United Nations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will continue to pursue efforts on this front.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Several Members, Mr Patrick Tay, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Louis Ng, Ms Joan Peirera, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Darryl David, asked whether there are plans to assist businesses, including our SMEs, and to educate the public on how to prevent and respond to cybersecurity threats and incidents.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Through the Cyber Security Awareness Alliance, CSA works closely with representatives from public and private sector organisations and industry associations to reach out to businesses, including SMEs, and to promote awareness and adoption of cybersecurity practices.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is done through organising cybersecurity talks and conferences and developing online cybersecurity resources, which are available on CSA’s GoSafeOnline website.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CSA also publishes an annual Singapore Cyber Landscape report for public awareness.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Besides these initiatives, businesses and members of the public can also sign up for SingCERT’s advisories and alerts on cybersecurity threats and incidents.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For example, when D-Link routers were found to have security vulnerabilities in September last year, SingCERT and the Info-communications Singapore Computer Emergency Response Team (ISG-CERT) under IMDA issued a joint advisory which contained information on the affected products and the steps that affected consumers should take.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CSA also collaborated with the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) to develop a series of Student Activity Books to raise awareness on the importance of Cybersecurity and Personal Data Protection among our students.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Silver Infocomm Junctions, an initiative by IMDA, provides seniors with infocomm training, which includes cybersecurity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will continue to work with partners in our efforts to raise cybersecurity awareness among the public.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad asked whether the Government could consider cybersecurity as another pillar of Total Defence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CSA has been working with MINDEF to incorporate cybersecurity messages in each of the existing five pillars of Total Defence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: On this, I agree with Ms Jessica Tan that people are the weakest link, but also our strongest asset.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Members also raised questions that do not relate directly to the Bill, but rather to the larger cybersecurity ecosystem that we are developing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I understand their concerns and agree that these are important issues to address.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As Mr Ganesh Rajaram mentioned, cybersecurity is not just the Government’s responsibility.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Everyone needs to play a role, including Members in this Chamber.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I hope that we can support the Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In particular, I would like to make special mention of Mr Chng Ho Kiat, Director of the Cybersecurity and Resilience Division in MCI, who passed away less than two weeks ago.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In his time at MCI, Ho Kiat made significant contributions towards the strengthening of cybersecurity in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: He played a pivotal role in developing the national cybersecurity strategy and this Bill.
